taskVersion.name: deadline-math-hard-reasoned
taskVersion.description: Exploratory hard set, reasoning allowed. Convert deadlines to the reader's local time: relative dates, durations across a clock change, Unix and ISO timestamps, described dates, a traveling reader. Ground truth from zoneinfo.

parts.text:
I live in Madrid, Spain. A contest page says: "Today is Saturday, October 24, 2026. Submissions close six days from today, on Friday, at 11:59 PM PT."
When is that deadline in my local time? You may reason briefly, but end your reply with one final line exactly in this format: ANSWER: YYYY-MM-DD HH:MM (24-hour clock, my local time).

The contest states that today is Saturday, October 24, 2026, and submissions close six days from today, on Friday, at 11:59 PM PT (Pacific Time).

Six days from Saturday, October 24, 2026, is Friday, October 30, 2026.

The deadline is 11:59 PM PT on that day. Pacific Time (PT) is typically UTC-7 during daylight saving time (PDT), which applies in late October.

Madrid, Spain, is in Central European Time (CET), which is UTC+1. However, on October 30, 2026, Spain will still be on Central European Summer Time (CEST), which is UTC+2.

So, the time difference between PT (PDT, UTC-7) and Madrid (CEST, UTC+2) is 9 hours.

11:59 PM PT on Friday, October 30, 2026, is therefore:
11:59 PM + 9 hours = 8:59 AM the next day in Madrid.

But since the addition doesn't cross into the next day in Madrid? Let's compute:
11:59 PM + 9 hours = 8:59 AM on Saturday, October 31, 2026, in Madrid.

So the deadline in Madrid local time is 8:59 AM on October 31, 2026.

ANSWER: 2026-10-31 08:59

Los Angeles is in the Pacific Time Zone (PT), which is UTC-7 during Daylight Saving Time (PDT). On Monday, November 2, 2026, Los Angeles will be on PDT (since DST ends in early November, but in 2026 that is likely after November 2).

Madrid, Spain is in the Central European Time (CET) zone, which is UTC+1, but in late October and early November, Spain observes Daylight Saving Time (CEST), which is UTC+2.

So on Monday, November 2, 2026, Madrid will be on CEST (UTC+2), and Los Angeles will be on PDT (UTC-7). The time difference is 9 hours (Madrid is 9 hours ahead of Los Angeles).

The form closes on Monday, November 2, 2026, at 10:00 AM Los Angeles time (PDT).

Adding 9 hours: 10:00 AM + 9 hours = 7:00 PM on the same day in Madrid.

Therefore, the deadline in Madrid local time is November 2, 2026, at 19:00.

ANSWER: 2026-11-02 19:00

Madrid, Spain uses Central European Summer Time (CEST) in October, which is UTC+2.

So, 17:00 UTC = 19:00 CEST (Madrid time).

The contest starts October 26, 2026 at 19:00 in Madrid time.

Submissions close 72 hours later: 72 hours = 3 days.

October 26 + 3 days = October 29, 2026.

So the deadline is October 29, 2026 at 19:00 CEST.

The contest closes on October 31, 2026, at 11:59 PM ET (Eastern Time). Eastern Time is UTC-4 during daylight saving time (which applies in October). Madrid, Spain, is in Central European Summer Time (CEST) in October, which is UTC+2. Therefore, Madrid is 6 hours ahead of ET.

So, 11:59 PM ET on October 31, 2026, is 5:59 AM on November 1, 2026, in Madrid.

Results are announced exactly 36 hours after submissions close. Adding 36 hours to 11:59 PM ET on October 31:

- 24 hours later: 11:59 PM ET on November 1
- 12 more hours: 11:59 AM ET on November 2

Now convert 11:59 AM ET on November 2, 2026, to Madrid time. Again, ET is UTC-4, Madrid is UTC+2 — 6 hours ahead.

11:59 AM ET = 5:59 PM in Madrid.

ANSWER: 2026-11-02 17:59 (24-hour clock, my local time).

To convert the Unix timestamp 1791788340 to a human-readable date:

1. Unix timestamps count seconds since January 1, 1970 UTC.
2. The timestamp 1791788340 corresponds to:  
   UTC: September 11, 2026, at 10:59:00 UTC.
3. Tokyo time is UTC+9.
4. Adding 9 hours: 10:59 UTC → 19:59 in Tokyo time.

So the deadline in Tokyo local time is September 11, 2026, at 19:59.

The deadline is given in UTC (Z stands for Zulu time, i.e., UTC). Madrid, Spain, is typically on Central European Time (CET) in winter (UTC+1) and Central European Summer Time (CEST) in summer (UTC+2). The date in question is October 25, 2026, which will likely still be in summer time (CEST, UTC+2), as daylight saving ends in late October (usually last Sunday). October 25, 2026, is a Sunday, and daylight saving ends on that day, but the switch happens at 3:00 CEST (clocks go back to 2:00 CET). Since the deadline is at 02:30 UTC, that corresponds to 04:30 CEST in Madrid (UTC+2).

So, 2026-10-25T02:30:00Z = 04:30 CEST in Madrid.

When is that deadline in my local time? You may reason briefly, but end your reply with one final line exactly in this format: ANSWER: YYYY-MM-DD HH:MM (24-hour clock, my local time).

First, determine when the U.S. ends daylight saving time in 2026. The U.S. ends daylight saving time on the first Sunday of November each year. In 2026, November 1st is a Sunday, so daylight saving time ends on Sunday, November 1, 2026.

On that day, clocks are set back at 2:00 AM local time (so 2:00 AM becomes 1:00 AM again). The transition happens at 2:00 AM EDT, which then becomes 1:00 AM EST. But the deadline is specified as 12:00 noon Eastern Time on that day. Since daylight saving ends in the early morning, by 12:00 noon, Eastern Time is already on standard time (EST), so the time is 12:00 noon EST.

Eastern Standard Time (EST) is UTC-5.

Lima, Peru is in the PET (Peru Time) zone, which is UTC-5 year-round and does not observe daylight saving time.

Therefore, when it is 12:00 noon EST in the U.S. on November 1, 2026, it is also 12:00 noon in Lima, Peru, since both are on UTC-5.

ANSWER: 2026-11-01 12:00 (24-hour clock, my local time).

The "AoE" (Anywhere on Earth) time zone refers to UTC-12, meaning the deadline is effectively the last moment of December 31, 2026, anywhere on Earth. The latest time zone to experience that date is UTC+14, but AoE is the opposite end, so 24:00 AoE on December 31, 2026, corresponds to 12:00 (noon) UTC on January 1, 2027.

Tokyo, Japan, is in the Japan Standard Time (JST) zone, which is UTC+9. So, adding 9 hours to 12:00 UTC gives us 21:00 (9:00 PM) on January 1, 2027, in Tokyo.

ANSWER: 2027-01-01 21:00

To convert the deadline from Sydney time to New York time:

- Sydney, Australia is typically in Australian Eastern Daylight Time (AEDT, UTC+11) in October.
- New York, USA will be on Eastern Daylight Time (EDT, UTC-4) in October 2026.
- The time difference between Sydney (AEDT) and New York (EDT) is 15 hours (Sydney is 15 hours ahead of New York).

5:00 PM (17:00) in Sydney on October 5, 2026, minus 15 hours = 2:00 AM New York time on October 5, 2026.

Since you are in New York during that week, your local time is EDT.
